decisions: Choose parity with sh rather than a full pwsh sandbox; keep pwsh file cmdlets and & ./script.ps1 unjudged. Sound scope.
Judge pwsh -Command and cmd /c or /k strings instead of refusing those wrappers. Sound, because it preserves legitimate use while matching sh wrappers.
Refuse script blocks rather than parse them, and direct sessions to the supported simplified cmdlets. Sound, because it keeps the change bounded and fail-closed.
Read exactly the two B40 forms: member property access on a parenthesized pipeline and literal $env assignments. Sound, targeted scope.
Judge cmd with the existing splitter and refuse % and ^ rather than parsing cmd fully. Sound for the advisory, fail-closed fence.
Apply W2-W4 to powershell calls and strings handed to powershell by W1, while sh -c remains POSIX and direct bash calls retain their current judgement.
Extend the configuration guide and fence audit; carry all user guidance in denial messages and change no skills.
Name pwsh, powershell -Command and cmd /c in fence help, document the pwsh eval and script-block refusal, and regenerate the command guide.
Leave Set-Content, Remove-Item, New-Item and & ./x.ps1 unchanged under the parity decision.
